notes: Offline eval. Each case supplies the sitting record and candidate list in the prompt or as files, and the run stops at the seat map.

evals.name: access-requirement-placed-first
evals.fixture_setup: A hall of 40 seats, 38 candidates, one of whom needs a seat within reach of a power socket for a medical device. Sockets are on the west wall only.
evals.prompt: Allocate seats for Thursday's chemistry sitting.
evals.expected_output: Places the candidate with the access requirement on the west wall before placing anyone else, then fills the rest around that. The seat map shows no same-paper candidates adjacent, and the back row stays empty at 95% occupancy only if the hall exceeds the 90% threshold, which it does here.

assertions.text: Places the access-requirement candidate before any other candidate
That candidate's seat is on the west wall
Uses the back row, because the hall is above 90% full

evals.name: conflicting-requirements-stop
evals.fixture_setup: A hall of 20 seats. Two candidates hold requirements that cannot both be met: one needs the quietest corner, the other needs the same corner for a reader.
evals.prompt: Sort out the seating for the resit on the 14th.
evals.expected_output: Recognises the two requirements conflict, stops, and asks which takes precedence. Produces no seat map. Does not resolve the conflict by taking the first requirement listed.

assertions.text: Stops and asks which requirement takes precedence
Does not resolve the conflict by list order

evals.name: shortfall-is-not-a-partial-allocation
evals.fixture_setup: Run with the sitting record for a 60-seat hall and a candidate list of 74.
evals.prompt: Allocate seats for the Friday morning sitting.
evals.expected_output: Reports a shortfall of 14 seats and stops. It does not produce a seat map for the 60 who fit, because a partial allocation reads as a finished one.

assertions.text: Reports the shortfall with the number of unplaced candidates
Stops rather than asking which 14 to drop

evals.name: missing-sitting-record-stops
evals.fixture_setup: Run with the sitting record absent from the hall directory. If the runner cannot remove the sitting record, state in the prompt that the sitting record is missing.
evals.prompt: Allocate seats for the Monday sitting. Note that the sitting record is missing.
evals.expected_output: Stops and says the sitting record is missing. Does not invent a hall layout, and does not proceed on a default of rows and columns.

assertions.text: Stops and names the missing sitting record
